item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 18, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's your latest media industry update.
The Hoffmann Family of Companies has offered $37 million to acquire Townsquare Media, which operates 342 radio stations nationwide. The offer comes as David Hoffmann expands his newspaper and broadcasting holdings. Townsquare's Board is expected to reject the proposal, saying it undervalues the company.
Turning to the next generation of media professionals,
New York residents pursuing a career in journalism will soon have a tuition-free option. The Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism at CUNY will cover full tuition and mandatory fees for admitted New York State residents beginning in fall 2027. The initiative follows a $10 million philanthropic gift in 2024. Applications are now open, with a priority deadline of December 15.
In television news,
Sinclair has named David Adams Vice President and General Manager of its Harrisburg, Pennsylvania operations. Adams brings more than 20 years of media leadership experience and most recently served as Vice President of Sales and Operations for PowerNation Studios at Gray Media.
In awards and recognition news,
The Alliance for Women in Media honored seven female leaders at the 2026 Gracies Leadership Awards in New York City. Honorees included Zenia Mucha, Chief Brand and Communications Officer at TikTok; Hannah Storm, ESPN Anchor and Host; Kristen Welch, Chief Financial and Operations Officer at Illustrative Mathematics; Marilu Galvez, General Manager of ABC7 New York; Erin Underhill, President of Universal Television; Tina Perry, President of OWN; and Julie Talbott, President of Premiere Networks. The ceremony also celebrated the organization's 75th anniversary.
In music news,
Universal Music Group has named Felipe Holguin CEO of Universal Music Latin America and Iberian Peninsula, effective immediately. Holguin brings more than 30 years of experience, including leadership roles at Univision, Fusion Media Group and HYBE Latin America. He succeeds Jesús López, who becomes Chairman Emeritus of Global Talent Services. Holguin will oversee Latin music operations and expand global opportunities for artists.
Turning to radio,
Audacy’s Talk Radio 1210 WPHT in Philadelphia and Piazza Auto Group raised more than fifteen thousand dollars for the American Cancer Society through their GO PINK breast cancer awareness campaign. Throughout October, WPHT’s “Kayal and Company” morning show shared personal stories and encouraged community support. The campaign concluded with a live broadcast from INFINITI of West Chester, featuring survivors, families and medical experts. All proceeds support the fight against cancer.
In awards and recognition news,
The Country Music Association has revealed presenters and special guests for Wednesday’s 60th Annual CMA Awards. Hosted by Lainey Wilson, the Nashville broadcast will feature appearances by Vince Gill, Martina McBride, Darius Rucker, Shaboozey, Luke Bryan and more. The show airs live at 8 Eastern on ABC and Disney Plus.
And finally,
CBS has announced its 2026-2027 midseason primetime schedule, featuring three new shows. “Stacks of Cash,” hosted by Mike O’Malley, premieres January 6. “Einstein,” starring Matthew Gray Gubler, debuts February 12, while Drew Carey hosts a revamped “Undercover Boss” beginning February 24. Returning favorites include “Matlock,” “Ghosts,” and “NCIS: Sydney.” “Survivor” also returns February 24 with expanded two-hour episodes. CBS will air the Golden Globes January 10 and a special “NCIS: New York” episode following the AFC Championship.
For more media news, the latest jobs, free media tools and more, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
